newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia lawmakers open probe of OAS chief Gaviria.
newsitem.headline: Colombia lawmakers open probe of OAS chief Gaviria.

text.p: Lawmakers have opened a preliminary investigation into possible misconduct by Cesar Gaviria, who served as Colombia's president from 1990-94, congressional sources said on Tuesday.

The sources confirmed a report in Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper that five congressmen had travelled to Washington over the weekend to question Gaviria, now secretary-general of the Organisation of American States, about numerous formal complaints lodged against him in Congress since he stepped down as president in August 1994.

The complaints include charges that Gaviria violated Colombia's sovereignty in 1993 when he authorised U.S. troops to carry out a so-called civic action programme involving the construction of a school and roadway in a jungle-covered area of southwest Valle province.

Gaviria faces similar violation of sovereignty charges, according to the congressional sources, for having authorised U.S. spy planes to overfly the infamous La Catedral prison in northwest Antioquia province, where late Medellin cartel drug boss Pablo Escobar was held in the lap of luxury from June 1991 until his escape in July 1992.

The palatial living conditions inside the La Catedral, which Escobar had custom built for him and from which he continued to run his criminal empire, sparked a public outcry when they finally became known after his escape.

The lawmakers who went to Washington are members of the Committee of Accusations of the House of Representatives, the same panel that investigated charges that President Ernesto Samper used drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
Committee members voted twice, by an overwhelming majority, to shelve that investigation.
